decision.final_answer:
MacBook Air and MacBook Pro product pages are both open (Air from step 2, Pro now at https://www.apple.com/macbook-pro/). From the US-English comparison block and Pro hero:

- Starting prices (US):
  - MacBook Air 13" and 15" (M5): from $1299
  - MacBook Pro 14" and 16" (M5 / M5 Pro / M5 Max): from $1999

- Available screen sizes:
  - MacBook Air: 13.6" or 15.3" display (marketed as 13" and 15")
  - MacBook Pro: 14.2" or 16.2" display (marketed as 14" and 16")

- Current base chip families:
  - MacBook Air: Apple M5 chip
  - MacBook Pro: Apple M5, M5 Pro, or M5 Max chips (family)

- Stated maximum battery life:
  - MacBook Air: up to 18 hours battery life
  - MacBook Pro: up to 24 hours battery life (longest battery life ever in a Mac)

Recommendation for a student (without configuring or purchasing):
- For most students (web, Office/Google Docs, note‑taking, light coding, streaming, light creative work), the MacBook Air is the better fit:
  - Much lower starting price ($1299 vs. $1999)
  - Still has the latest Apple M5 chip and up to 18 hours of battery life, which already covers a full day of classes and study
  - Lighter, more portable with 13.6" and 15.3" options
- Choose a MacBook Pro only if the student expects sustained heavy workloads like 3D graphics, video editing, music production with many tracks, or intensive AI / data-science work, where:
  - The more advanced M5 Pro / M5 Max options, larger 14.2"/16.2" displays, more ports, and up to 24 hours of battery life justify the much higher cost and slightly heavier machine.

Given a typical student use case and price sensitivity, the recommended choice is MacBook Air (M5), with screen size chosen based on their preference for portability (13.6") vs. workspace (15.3").
